items.question_text: You need to host an application on a Compute Engine instance in a project shared with other teams. You want to prevent the other teams from accidentally causing downtime on that application. Which feature should you use?
items.solution_text: Deletion protection is the specific feature designed to prevent Compute Engine instances from being accidentally deleted by users with the compute.instances.delete permission. While Shielded VMs focus on security against rootkits and sole-tenant nodes provide physical isolation, neither prevents operational mistakes like deletion. Preemptible VMs actually increase downtime risk due to their nature, making deletion protection the correct control for this scenario.

choices.text: Use a Shielded VM.
Use a Preemptible VM.
Use a sole-tenant node.
Enable deletion protection on the instance.

items.question_text: Your organization needs to grant users access to query datasets in BigQuery but prevent them from accidentally deleting the datasets. You want a solution that follows Google-recommended practices. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
Option D is the correct answer because it strictly adheres to Google Cloud IAM best practices by using groups rather than individual users for role assignment, which simplifies policy management and reduces drift.
While pre-defined roles are generally preferred, none of them perfectly match the requirement to query without *any* ability to create datasets (which grants Data Owner permissions allowing deletion).
Therefore, a custom role tailored to remove delete/create permissions and assigned to a group is the most secure and manageable solution.

choices.text: Add users to roles/bigquery user role only, instead of roles/bigquery dataOwner.
Add users to roles/bigquery dataEditor role only, instead of roles/bigquery dataOwner.
Create a custom role by removing delete permissions, and add users to that role only.
Create a custom role by removing delete permissions. Add users to the group, and then add the group to the custom role.

items.question_text: You have a developer laptop with the Cloud SDK installed on Ubuntu. The Cloud SDK was installed from the Google Cloud Ubuntu package repository. You want to test your application locally on your laptop with Cloud Datastore. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
When the Cloud SDK is installed via a package manager like APT on Ubuntu, the gcloud component manager is disabled by design.
Therefore, attempting to use 'gcloud components install' (Option D) will fail with an error indicating that the component manager is not available for this installation method.
To install the Datastore emulator in this environment, you must use the system package manager with 'apt-get install google-cloud-sdk-datastore-emulator' as specified in Option C.

choices.text: Export Cloud Datastore data using gcloud datastore export.
Create a Cloud Datastore index using gcloud datastore indexes create.
Install the google-cloud-sdk-datastore-emulator component using the apt get install command.
Install the cloud-datastore-emulator component using the gcloud components install command.

items.question_text: Your company set up a complex organizational structure on Google Cloud. The structure includes hundreds of folders and projects. Only a few team members should be able to view the hierarchical structure. You need to assign minimum permissions to these team members, and you want to follow Google-recommended practices. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
To follow Google-recommended practices for identity management, permissions should be assigned to groups rather than individual users.

The `roles/browser` role is the correct minimal permission set because it explicitly grants read access to browse the resource hierarchy (folders, projects, and organization structure) without granting access to view specific resource data or IAM policy details beyond browsing.

choices.text: Add the users to roles/browser role.
Add the users to roles/iam.roleViewer role.
Add the users to a group, and add this group to roles/browser.
Add the users to a group, and add this group to roles/iam.roleViewer role.

items.question_text: Your company has a single sign-on (SSO) identity provider that supports Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) integration with service providers. Your company has users in Cloud Identity. You would like users to authenticate using your company's SSO provider. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
The scenario requires users to authenticate via the company's existing SSO provider, making it the Identity Provider (IdP) and Google Cloud Identity the Service Provider (SP). In this SAML federation model, Cloud Identity consumes the authentication assertion from the third-party IdP.
Option B correctly describes configuring a third-party IdP with Google as the SP, whereas Option A incorrectly reverses these roles.

choices.text: In Cloud Identity, set up SSO with Google as an identity provider to access custom SAML apps.
In Cloud Identity, set up SSO with a third-party identity provider with Google as a service provider.
Obtain OAuth 2.0 credentials, configure the user consent screen, and set up OAuth 2.0 for Mobile & Desktop Apps.
Obtain OAuth 2.0 credentials, configure the user consent screen, and set up OAuth 2.0 for Web Server Applications.
